nodes.summary: EMC is a frontend-only ExC Shell SPA with no backend repo; all mutations and queries call external Adobe APIs (ESP, ESL) directly through a centralized ApiService with caching, validation, and dry-run support.
nodes.details: EMC (web-src/src/) is a React 18 + TypeScript + React Spectrum S2 SPA deployed via Adobe App Builder. There is no backend in this repo. All API calls route through services/api.ts (ApiService) and cachedApi wrapper: GET requests use 10s caching with request dedup and pattern-based invalidation; all mutations require input validation via validateString()/validateObject() before dispatch; all fetch calls pass through safeFetch() with ALLOWED_HOSTS validation. Two external backends: Adobe ESP (events/series/speakers endpoints) and ESL (lifecycle/venues/attendees). Auth uses Bearer token (IMS in prod, dev token locally) + x-gw-ims-org-id header. Dry-run mode available via apiService.enableDryRun(). Form state (EventForm, SeriesForm) persists to sessionStorage with debounced auto-save; multi-step FormWizard uses useEventFormComponent hook lifecycle (onGatherPayload, onAfterSave, onLoadResponse, validate) for step registration.

nodes.summary: Session registration UI follows a three-state model (Registered/Waitlisted, Able to Register, Blocked) with explicit predicates for each state; SessionTimeFull responses must be read from body, not just HTTP status.
nodes.details: In `event-libs/v1/blocks/sessions-hub/sessions-hub.js`, the per-card CTA must implement exactly three states: (1) Registered/Waitlisted badge (blue, shows checkmark + text from `waitlist-cta-text` dictionary key, hover swaps to unregister action), (2) Able-to-register button (direct `registerForSessionTime` API call, no modal), (3) Blocked button (disabled `.sh-btn-blocked`, labeled from `Registration unavailable` dictionary key). Use `isSessionTimeFullError(resp)` helper to detect SessionTimeFull errors by checking `error.code | errorCode | error | type | message` fields defensively. Event-level waitlist state (`rsvpData.registrationStatus === 'waitlisted'`) blocks all per-card registration; event-closed state (computed from `isFull && !allowWaitlisting`, accepting both boolean and string `'true'`) also blocks. Banner visibility: keep visible for waitlisted users (only hide when `isEventRegistered === true`), render `sh-banner-waitlist-msg` paragraph with `getEventWaitlistBannerMessage(manager, { eventTitle })` helper from `dictionary-manager.js`.

nodes.summary: EMC centralizes all API calls through a singleton ApiService class with consistent error handling, authentication management, and mock-to-real API switching via config.json action URLs.
nodes.details: All external API calls route through ApiService.callAction<T>(actionName, params, method) in /web-src/src/services/api.ts. Authentication is set once via apiService.setAuthHeaders(token, org) and applied to all requests. Backend URLs are configured via apiService.setActionUrls(urls) from config.json, enabling mock-to-real switching without code changes: remove mock import, update the method to call this.callAction('actionName'), and add the URL to config.json actions object. Mock data lives in /web-src/src/mocks/ as TypeScript modules exporting both data and Promise-returning functions (with 300ms delay to simulate latency). This pattern decouples frontend from backend readiness and enables parallel development.

nodes.summary: EMC frontend organizes event form as 13 modular components under EventForm/ directory, each owning a logical section (venue, speakers, agenda, etc.), composed by EventForm.tsx wizard container.
nodes.details: The EventForm/ directory contains 13 specialized components (EventFormatComponent, EventInfoComponent, VenueComponent, SpeakersComponent, SponsorsComponent, AgendaComponent, EventImagesComponent, ProfilesComponent, RegistrationConfigComponent, RegistrationFieldsComponent, PageMetadataComponent, plus index.ts barrel export) that are composed into a multi-step wizard by the parent EventForm.tsx container. Each component owns a logical domain (e.g., VenueComponent handles Google Places integration, SpeakersComponent manages speaker CRUD, RegistrationFieldsComponent configures RSVP form fields). This modular decomposition enables independent testing, reuse, and maintenance of form sections. The barrel export (index.ts) centralizes imports for the parent wizard.

nodes.summary: Dev token system is gated by both URL query parameter (?devtokenmode=true) and host allowlist (localhost or approved dev instances); without the parameter, the UI button is hidden and stored tokens are not used for API calls.
nodes.details: The dev token feature in EMC requires two conditions to be active: (1) the URL must include ?devtokenmode=true and (2) the host must be localhost or an approved dev instance (e.g., 14257-emc-dev.adobeio-static.net). When both conditions are met, the Dev Token button appears in the top-right UI and API calls use the stored token via tokenStorage.getValidToken(). When running in Adobe Experience Cloud Shell, the real IMS token is automatically used instead and the dev token button never appears. API calls should use constructRequestHeaders(token) and safeFetch() helpers to inject the token into request headers.

nodes.summary: Production event publishing requires explicit user confirmation via AlertDialog before calling publishEvent; dev/stage builds skip this gate.
nodes.details: In EventForm.tsx, when ENVIRONMENT=prod, both handleComplete and executeSaveWithUrl paths funnel through requestPublishAfterUrlResolved, which opens a Spectrum 2 AlertDialog for user acceptance before invoking publishEvent. nodes.summary: Event speaker PUT request body must be contract-shaped; do not spread raw GET response into PUT payload.
nodes.details: The API service layer enforces a specific payload shape for speaker PUT operations (web-src/src/services/api.ts). When updating event speakers, construct the request body to match the server's expected contract rather than spreading the GET response directly. This prevents field mismatches and validation failures. See Sessions and EventForm components for correct usage patterns.

nodes.summary: Attendee API field `requiresTicket` is the canonical name; prior `requiresSxswTicket` was renamed across routes, manager, and OpenAPI spec as part of generalization.

nodes.summary: Do not omit server modification time (mtime) when updating session-time API without page refresh; failure to persist and send mtime in consecutive calls triggers OptimisticLockExceptionError.
nodes.details: The session-time API endpoint requires the server's modification timestamp (mtime) to be stored after each response and included in subsequent PUT/PATCH requests. Omitting mtime causes the server to reject the update as a stale write. Additionally, ensure POST is only called once during session creation; subsequent updates must use PUT/PATCH with the cached mtime to avoid duplicate session-time records.

nodes.summary: RSVP registration payloads must include `requiresSxswTicket` flag and implicit consent via `contactMethods` field; sanitize HTML in form text/textarea inputs and enforce RSVP limit column as maxlength constraint.
nodes.details: When submitting event-attendee payloads for RSVP, include `requiresSxswTicket` boolean when SXSW ticket filter applies (#140). Implicit consent for new registrations is recorded via the `contactMethods` field in the payload (MWPW-194036, #126). In events-form block (event-libs/v1/blocks/events-form/events-form.js), sanitize HTML in text and textarea inputs (#110) and honor the RSVP limit column value as the `maxlength` attribute constraint. These patterns ensure consistent registration data shape and prevent XSS while respecting capacity limits.

nodes.summary: Event Form uses 4-step wizard structure where Step 1 groups 5 logical components (format, tags, info, dates, venue) rather than separating into individual steps; this matches v1 reference and improves UX.
nodes.details: The EventForm wizard in EMC follows a deliberate 4-step structure (not 8) where Step 1 contains EventFormatComponent, Tags, Event Info, Date/Time, and Venue components as logical sub-sections. This pattern groups related fields (e.g., all basic event metadata in Step 1) while keeping the overall flow concise. Step 2 handles Speakers/Hosts, Step 3 handles images, Step 4 handles RSVP/status. When implementing new event forms or extending this wizard, maintain this grouping: do not split Step 1 into separate steps unless UX research shows users abandon multi-step forms at >6 steps. The FormWizard shared component manages progress tracking and navigation across all steps.

nodes.summary: Silent failures in Splash attendee status updates (PUT /external/events/:id/attendees/:id) due to missing externalAttendeeId → attendeeId mappings caused EMC/Splash count mismatches; resolved via direct DynamoDB correction.
nodes.details: When Splash sends status updates via PUT /external/events/:id/attendees/:id without a valid externalAttendeeId → attendeeId mapping in the service layer, the request fails silently rather than returning an error, leaving EMC counts stale while Splash reflects the true state. This caused deltas of 135+ waitlisted and 80+ declined records. Future agents should: (1) audit the attendee mapping lookup logic in the PUT handler to ensure it returns explicit errors on missing mappings rather than silently skipping updates, (2) add monitoring/alerting on PUT /external/events/:id/attendees/:id response codes to catch similar silent failures early, (3) recognize that zzTest migration scripts in this repo are the canonical runbook for data reconciliation when such mismatches occur.

nodes.summary: ESP OpenAPI spec must define response schemas for all HTTP status codes returned by endpoints, including 200; missing schemas cause runtime validation failures.
nodes.details: The events-service-platform validates responses against the OpenAPI spec at runtime. If an endpoint returns a 200 status code but the spec lacks a schema definition for that code, the request fails with 'no schema defined for status code' error. This applies to POST /v1/events/{eventId}/attendees and all other endpoints. Always add response schema definitions (including status code, content-type, and body shape) to src/api/openapi.json when adding or modifying endpoints, even for success cases.

nodes.summary: RSVP button and form 400-error handling must respect campaign capacity when ?campaign URL param is present and valid, falling back to event capacity otherwise, with campaign-specific error messages and UI state.

nodes.summary: Session Page is the durable standalone page per session at /sessions/[slug]-[code].html, the permanent on-demand destination

nodes.details: The auto-registration flow is now owned by the events-form block, which receives session context via BlockMediator. The isAutoRegistrationEnabled flag must be evaluated at form-submission time (not at block-init time) to correctly detect when a user is already registered in a conflicting session. See esp-controller.js and events-form.js for the BlockMediator handoff pattern and the timing of the registration-state check.

nodes.summary: Optimistic concurrency via modificationTime prevents lost updates on concurrent event edits
nodes.details: Implemented by be-agent-events: Every PUT /events/:id requires a modificationTime field matching the server's last-known value. If they differ, the update returns 409 Conflict with the current server state. The frontend shows a diff dialog allowing the user to merge or overwrite. This pattern prevents the classic 'last write wins' problem when two admins edit the same event.

nodes.summary: Client-side date validation without timezone awareness caused events to appear with wrong dates for cross-timezone organizers
nodes.details: Reported by qa-agent-events: The event creation form validated dates using JavaScript Date() which uses the browser's local timezone. An organizer in PST creating a Tokyo event entered '2026-06-15' as the start date, but the API received '2026-06-14T07:00:00Z' due to timezone offset. Fix: all date inputs explicitly paired with timezone selector, validation runs against the event's timezone, not the browser's.

nodes.summary: Session-times entities must have exactly one location; location is a required, singular property of the session-times schema, not a separate join table.
nodes.details: Per the PR note, location support was added directly to the session-times schema (src/managers/sessionTimesMgr.js, src/api/openapi.json) as a one-to-one relationship: 'a session-times entity should have one and only one location associated.' This means session-times CRUD operations (create, read, update, delete in src/routes/session-times/) must always include location data; location is not optional and should not be managed as a separate entity reference. Strict API validation (unevaluated fields rejected) enforces this contract at the API boundary.

nodes.summary: Parallel API queries for attendee status types are merged into a single result set; new status types require only type union updates and StatusBadge entries, not table/filter/export logic changes.
nodes.details: In EMC's Registrations page, attendee statuses (registered, waitlisted, declined) are fetched via parallel `?type=X` queries in `getAllEventAttendees()` (web-src/src/services/api.ts) and merged into a single `AttendeeStats` result. Adding a new status requires: (1) extending the `RegistrationStatus` union, (2) adding a `StatusBadge` variant entry (web-src/src/components/shared/StatusBadge.tsx), and (3) updating `AttendeeStats` interface. Table rendering, filtering, and CSV export are data-driven and automatically support new statuses without code changes.

nodes.summary: Invite-only events without a valid campaign parameter must block RSVP UI and show a shared dictionary-driven message across all event blocks (decorate, events-form, sessions-hub).
nodes.details: When an invite-only event is opened without a valid `campaign` URL parameter, the RSVP flow is blocked. Use `dictionaryManager.getInviteOnlyNoCampaignMessage()` to fetch the user-facing message from the dictionary sheet. In sessions-hub, compute `inviteOnlyBlocked` after `await dictionaryManager.initialize()`, then replace the sticky Register CTA and per-card event-registration buttons with the status message. Guard all click handlers and sessionStorage-deferred modal opens to prevent RSVP submission. Apply CSS classes `.sh-banner-invite-only-msg` and `.sh-invite-only-msg` for styling. This pattern ensures parity across decorate.js, events-form.js, and sessions-hub.js.

nodes.summary: Campaign-aware RSVP registration: when campaignId URL param is present, fetch campaign capacity and apply waitlist rules before attendee creation.
nodes.details: In esp-controller.js, the getAndCreateAndAddAttendee flow checks for campaignId in the attendee payload. If present and event is not full, call getCampaign(eventId, campaignId) to fetch campaign capacity (attendeeLimit, attendeeCount, waitlistAttendeeCount). Apply waitlist logic: if attendeeLimit === attendeeCount, mark waitlisted; if attendeeLimit > attendeeCount and waitlistAttendeeCount > 0, mark waitlisted; if attendeeLimit > attendeeCount and waitlistAttendeeCount === 0, register normally. If no attendeeLimit, pass campaignId without campaign logic. Skip campaign lookup when event is already full. campaignId is sanitized in events-form.js (regex ^[\w-]{1,128}$) and added to EVENT_ATTENDEE_DATA_FILTER in data-utils.js so it flows into the event attendee API body.

nodes.summary: Channel, Session Guide, and Session Page defined as three distinct entities with explicit routing contracts for the event UX
nodes.details: Decision by aseghi (May 2026): Three entities — Channel, Session Guide, Session Page — are distinct UX components. Routing: Session Guide organizes sessions by Channel. Live session in Session Guide → Watch Now → Channel on Homepage. On-demand session in Session Guide → Session Page. Session Page Live state → Watch Now → Channel. Post-event: Session Guide at /sessions.html, cards → Session Page. Session Scheduling Agent supplements Session Guide (does not replace it), syncs to Rainfocus My Sessions. Entity definitions in Session Guide PRD (wiki/3746198038), Session Pages PRD (wiki/3872870192), Scheduling Agent PRD (wiki/3872870197).

nodes.summary: Sessions tab in Event Report uses lazy-loaded expandable rows to display per-session attendee lists, cross-referencing session-time attendees with event attendees for display names.

Attendee display names are resolved by cross-referencing the session-time attendee list against the parent event's attendee roster. SessionTimeInfo type extends with attendeeCount, waitlistAttendeeCount, isFull fields. Expanded state resets when switching events to avoid stale data.

nodes.summary: Session Guide is the consolidated session discovery layer on the Homepage, replacing Sessions Hub, Agenda, and My Schedule

Four views: All Sessions (organized by Channel), My Sessions (schedule + .ics download + AI agent entry), My Favorites (T1 only), On Demand (T1 only). Routes to Channel Homepage experience when a session is live; routes to Session Page when on-demand. Post-event: accessible as full page at /sessions.html — session cards route to Session Pages; modals retired.

nodes.summary: Detect session description truncation via DOM layout (scrollHeight vs clientHeight) rather than character limits; re-sync on filter, expand/collapse, font load, and resize events.
nodes.details: In sessions-hub.js, replace fixed-character truncation logic with dynamic overflow detection: compare element.scrollHeight > element.clientHeight to determine if text is truncated. Export syncSessionDescriptionsOverflow() and call it after filter changes, expand/collapse toggles, fonts ready (via document.fonts.ready), and ResizeObserver triggers. This ensures descriptions adapt to actual layout constraints (viewport, font metrics, container width) rather than hardcoded thresholds. Apply the same sync pattern to the conflict modal: defer modal close until registration completes, show pending state on confirm button and option elements, and restore UI on failure.

nodes.summary: Invite-only events gate RSVP behind `inviteOnly` flag and campaign URL param; replace button with text message rather than disable.
nodes.details: The invite-only RSVP feature gates registration on two conditions: (1) an `inviteOnly` event flag from the backend, and (2) a campaign URL parameter. When both conditions are met, the RSVP button is replaced with a text message instead of being disabled. This pattern prevents accidental user confusion and clarifies that the event is not available for self-service registration. Check `event-libs/v1/blocks/events-form/events-form.js` for the gating logic and button replacement implementation.

nodes.summary: Session-time helpers must return SessionTimeInfo so React state can update without a page refresh
nodes.details: createSessionTimeForSession and upsertSessionTimeForSession previously returned Promise<void>, which dropped the API's sessionTimeId, creationTime, and modificationTime on the floor. Calling components could not update local state with the new optimistic-concurrency values, so users saw stale data and had to refresh the page after every session-time edit. Fix is to return the API response from both helpers and have handleAddSession / handleUpdateSession capture and propagate sessionTimeId + creationTime + modificationTime into local React session state. This is the EMC-wide convention for any API helper that yields server-issued timestamps.

nodes.summary: Do not spread GET response into PUT body; construct narrow association payloads with only required fields plus timestamps.
nodes.details: In `web-src/src/services/api.ts`, `updateSpeakerInEvent` previously merged the full GET response (minus `creationTime`) into the PUT body, sending unintended fields to ESP. The corrected pattern: construct PUT payloads with only `speakerId`, `speakerType`, `ordinal` (from caller patch with GET fallbacks when omitted), plus `creationTime` and `modificationTime` from GET. This matches the documented ESP contract and the existing `updateSponsorInEvent` pattern. Callers like the Speakers dashboard may send partial patches (e.g., only `speakerId`); the service must fill missing association fields from the prior GET before PUT.

nodes.summary: ESP event-speaker PUT body contract is { speakerId, speakerType, ordinal, creationTime, modificationTime } and nothing else
nodes.details: Per ESP OpenAPI, /v1/events/:eventId/speakers/:speakerId PUT accepts only those five fields. Echoing the full GET response (spreading dependentData) fails server-side validation and has been the root cause of repeated 400s on edit. When using callWithDependency's body-builder, fall back to dependentData per-field: body.X ?? dependentData.X. creationTime and modificationTime are server-issued; do not let callers override them. The same pattern applies to all ESP PUTs on speaker resources.

nodes.summary: Do not omit server modification time (mtime) when updating session-time API without page refresh; failure to persist and send mtime in consecutive calls triggers OptimisticLockExceptionError.
nodes.details: The session-time API endpoint requires the server's modification timestamp (mtime) to be stored after each response and included in subsequent PUT/PATCH requests. When session-time params are updated in-memory without a page refresh, the mtime must be extracted from the server response and cached in component state (e.g., Sessions.tsx) so it is available for the next API call. Omitting mtime causes the server to reject the update as a stale write. Additionally, ensure POST is only called once during session creation; subsequent updates must use PUT/PATCH with the cached mtime to avoid duplicate session-time records.

nodes.summary: ESP resources use modificationTime for optimistic concurrency on PUT; clients must round-trip it
nodes.details: Every ESP PUT on an updatable resource (event, series, session, speaker) requires the modificationTime field to match the server's last-known value. If they differ, PUT returns 409 with the current server state. Clients must therefore: (a) capture modificationTime on every GET, (b) send it back unchanged on the next PUT, (c) re-fetch on 409 and merge. Dropping or recomputing modificationTime client-side is the most common cause of silent edit failures on EMC.

nodes.summary: Sessions tab in Event Report uses lazy-loaded expandable rows to display per-session attendee lists, cross-referencing session-time attendees with event attendees for display names.
nodes.details: The Sessions registration tab (SessionsTab.tsx) implements a table with expandable rows that lazy-load attendee data via getSessionTimeAttendees(timeId) from GET /v1/session-times/{timeId}/attendees. Attendee display names are resolved by cross-referencing the session-time attendee list against the parent event's attendee roster. SessionTimeInfo type extends with attendeeCount, waitlistAttendeeCount, isFull fields. Expanded state resets when switching events to avoid stale data.

nodes.summary: Optimistic concurrency via modificationTime prevents lost updates on concurrent event edits
nodes.details: Implemented by be-agent-events: Every PUT /events/:id requires a modificationTime field matching the server's last-known value. If they differ, the update returns 409 Conflict with the current server state. The frontend shows a diff dialog allowing the user to merge or overwrite. This pattern prevents the classic 'last write wins' problem when two admins edit the same event.

nodes.summary: Orphaned page cleanup is triggered synchronously at Kinesis record-processing time by detecting detailPagePath changes via event history, not deferred to the handler loop.
nodes.details: When a published, liveUpdate event is modified, EventDataStreamProcessor calls EventService.getEventHistory(eventId) to fetch the event's prior states. findLastPublishedHistory walks the history array newest-to-oldest, skipping entries whose timestamp matches the current modificationTime (race-condition guard), and returns the first entry with published=true && liveUpdate=true. If that entry's detailPagePath differs from the current one, sendEventDataToWebhook is called immediately with isDeleteEvent=true and the old path, allowing downstream consumers (e.g. SharePoint) to clean up orphaned pages without waiting for the main handler. History fetch failures are caught and logged; processing continues normally (no Kinesis retry). Timestamp comparison uses String() coercion on both sides to handle type differences between DynamoDB-unmarshalled numbers and history API values.

nodes.summary: Do not replace entire itemData objects in DynamoDB PUT operations without preserving required fields; use merge/patch semantics or enforce all required fields in the request schema.
nodes.details: Publishing profiles were created with status: 'active', but PUT /v1/publishing-profiles/{profileId} requests that omitted status would replace the entire stored itemData, removing the field. This caused later GET /v1/events/{eventId}/publishing-profiles responses to fail OpenAPI validation (418 error) because status is a required field on PublishingProfile schema. Fix: (1) add defensive fallback in profile read paths to return status: 'active' if missing, (2) make status required on PublishingProfileUpdateRequest schema to prevent future drops, (3) ensure PublishingProfile response schema enforces status as required. This pattern applies to all DynamoDB-backed resources where PUT replaces rather than merges.

nodes.summary: Do not use Kinesis payload as source of truth for event metadata; always rehydrate from DynamoDB on every stream record, even for localization-only updates.
nodes.details: EMC emits two Kinesis records per event save (one for event, one for localization), but only the first carries full metadata (e.g., cloud-type). In EventDataStreamProcessor.js processRecord(), the prior logic conditionally rehydrated from DynamoDB only when liveUpdate=true, causing localization records to forward partial payloads downstream. This broke `.page` preview RSVP forms when the second (partial) write overwrote the first (complete) write. Fix: always rebuild newData.itemData from liveData (DynamoDB), falling back to Kinesis payload only for localizations and localizationOverrides fields. This ensures both eventData and localization Kinesis records produce fully hydrated payloads to Hoolihan/AIO DA.

nodes.summary: Image metadata updates are decoupled from image upload via a dedicated PATCH endpoint, allowing clients to enrich metadata (e.g., add sharepointUrl) post-upload without re-uploading the binary.
nodes.details: The `/v1/events/{eventId}/images/{imageId}/metadata` PATCH endpoint (src/routes/events/images/metadata/update.js) enables clients to update image metadata fields like sharepointUrl after the image binary has already been stored in S3. This decoupling prevents unnecessary re-uploads and allows asynchronous enrichment workflows (e.g., waiting for SharePoint processing before linking). The ImageService and S3Service handle the separation of concerns: S3Service manages binary storage, ImageService manages metadata state. Future endpoints that accept binary + metadata should follow this two-step pattern when metadata may arrive later.

nodes.summary: Image upload handlers for resource entities (events, speakers, sponsors) must extend AbstractResourceService to inherit standardized image CRUD logic and avoid duplication.
nodes.details: Events, Speakers, and Sponsors all require POST/PUT/DELETE image endpoints with identical validation and payload handling. Rather than duplicate logic across EventService, SpeakerService, and SponsorService, extract common image operations into AbstractResourceService base class. Each service extends this base and inherits create.js, update.js, delete.js route handlers that call prepareImagePayload() and service methods. This pattern ensures consistent error handling (e.g., fixing the 500 error on sponsor image upload) and reduces maintenance surface. Apply this pattern to any new resource type that needs image management.

nodes.summary: EMC frontend organizes event form as 13 modular components under EventForm/ directory, each owning a logical section (venue, speakers, agenda, etc.), composed by EventForm.tsx wizard container.
nodes.details: The EventForm/ directory contains 13 specialized components (EventFormatComponent, EventInfoComponent, VenueComponent, SpeakersComponent, SponsorsComponent, AgendaComponent, EventImagesComponent, ProfilesComponent, RegistrationConfigComponent, RegistrationFieldsComponent, PageMetadataComponent, plus index.ts barrel export) that are composed into a multi-step wizard by the parent EventForm.tsx container. Each component owns a logical domain (e.g., VenueComponent handles Google Places integration, SpeakersComponent manages speaker CRUD, RegistrationFieldsComponent configures RSVP form fields). This modular decomposition enables independent testing, reuse, and maintenance of form sections. The barrel export (index.ts) centralizes imports for the parent wizard.

nodes.summary: Event Form uses 4-step wizard structure where Step 1 groups 5 logical components (format, tags, info, dates, venue) rather than separating into individual steps; this matches v1 reference and improves UX.
nodes.details: The EventForm wizard in EMC follows a deliberate 4-step structure (not 8) where Step 1 contains EventFormatComponent, Tags, Event Info, Date/Time, and Venue components as logical sub-sections. This pattern groups related fields (e.g., all basic event metadata in Step 1) while keeping the overall flow concise. Step 2 handles Speakers/Hosts, Step 3 handles images, Step 4 handles RSVP/status. When implementing new event forms or extending this wizard, maintain this grouping: do not split Step 1 into separate steps unless UX research shows users abandon multi-step forms at >6 steps. The FormWizard shared component manages progress tracking and navigation across all steps.

nodes.summary: When hydrating event payloads from DynamoDB kinesis records with sk=localizations, source seriesId and detailPagePath from the pre-fetched liveData object, not from newData.itemData (which lacks these fields).
nodes.details: In EventDataStreamProcessor.js, when processing a localization record change (sk=localizations), the newData.itemData payload contains only localizations and localizationOverrides. To build a complete hydrated event for ESL, pull seriesId and detailPagePath from liveData (fetched via eventService.getEventData at processRecord start), not from newData.itemData. This is safe because EventService.updateVenue writes the new detailPagePath to DynamoDB before the venue record fires the kinesis stream, ensuring liveData.detailPagePath is current. Omitting these fields causes DA webhook page creation to fail or write to wrong locations.

nodes.summary: Speaker photo hydration requires explicit imagesMgr.list() join; photos are stored as separate DynamoDB records (sk: imagekind#speaker-photo) and must be fetched and attached to speaker objects.
nodes.details: In src/routes/events/speakers/read.js, both GET /v1/events/:eventId/speakers (list) and GET /v1/events/:eventId/speakers/:speakerId (single) endpoints must call imagesMgr.list() in parallel and join photo records onto speaker objects by matching speaker ID. This pattern is already correctly implemented in GET /v1/series/:seriesId/speakers and should be mirrored across all speaker-returning endpoints. Speakers without uploaded photos should return without a photo field (not null or error). Omitting this hydration step leaves the photo field missing from the response contract.

nodes.summary: Attendees resource has dual CRUD surfaces: standalone /v1/attendees/* for lifecycle management, and nested /v1/events/:eventId/attendees/* for event-specific membership operations only.
nodes.details: The attendees CRUD operations split across two route hierarchies: /v1/attendees/{create,read,update,delete}.js handle attendee entity lifecycle (create new attendee, read attendee details, update attendee profile, delete attendee). The nested /v1/events/:eventId/attendees/* routes (in src/routes/events/attendees/) handle only event membership: POST adds an *existing* attendee to an event (does not create attendees), GET lists attendees for an event, DELETE removes attendee from event, PUT updates attendee's event-specific state. This separation prevents attendee creation from being coupled to event enrollment. Enforce via attendeesMgr.js and eventsMgr.js: standalone routes call attendeesMgr directly; nested routes validate attendee exists before calling eventsMgr membership methods.

nodes.summary: Manager classes in events-service-platform automatically persist request body fields via spread operator; schema changes alone are sufficient for new optional fields without code changes.
nodes.details: The `sponsorsMgr.js` manager spreads the full request body into `itemData` during POST/PUT operations, meaning any new optional field added to OpenAPI schemas (e.g., `ordinal` in EventSponsorCreateBody, EventSponsorUpdateBody) is automatically persisted and returned without requiring manager code changes. This pattern applies to sponsor creation, updates, and retrieval. When adding optional fields to event entities, verify the manager uses spread semantics before adding schema-only changes.

nodes.summary: All DELETE endpoints return 204 No Content; all database managers export singleton instances; event images are a first-class resource with full CRUD routes.
nodes.details: DELETE operations across all routes (eventSeries/delete.js, events/delete.js, events/attendees/delete.js, events/speakers/delete.js, events/images/delete.js) now return HTTP 204 No Content instead of 200 with an empty array. All manager classes in src/managers/ (attendeesMgr.js, eventsMgr.js, seriesMgr.js, speakersMgr.js, venuesMgr.js) export a singleton instance rather than the class itself, requiring route handlers to call methods on the exported instance. Event images are now a managed resource with dedicated CRUD routes (src/routes/events/images/) backed by database implementation in eventsMgr.js.

nodes.summary: Webhook handlers must validate x-provider-identity header before processing provider-specific payloads to prevent cross-provider data corruption.
nodes.details: The splashthat-esl webhook update handler (src/routes/webhooks/splashthat-esl/update.js) now validates the x-provider-identity header before delegating to SplashThatProvider.js. This prevents malformed or misrouted webhook payloads (e.g., event_type_id as string '81125' instead of number) from corrupting event settings. The check acts as a gating mechanism upstream of the provider-specific payload transformation logic, catching identity mismatches before they reach the updateSettings call that enforces strict schema validation.

nodes.summary: MPS integration manager handles marketing consent transmission and service-token generation with deferred routing integration pending guest-checkout flow.
nodes.details: The `mpsMgr.js` module in events-service-platform encapsulates two responsibilities: (1) sending marketing communication permissions to MPS, distinguishing implicit vs. explicit consent flows, and (2) generating and caching service tokens for the ESP client ID `acom_event_service`. The manager is implemented but not yet wired into `src/routes/attendees/create.js` because it depends on a pending guest-checkout flow. The current contract expects request bodies to include `consentId` and `contactMethod` (comma-separated channel list for explicit consent); these field names are subject to change pending stakeholder review (cc @cod87753). Future integrators should treat this as a blocking dependency on guest-checkout completion before routing attendee-create requests through mpsMgr.

nodes.summary: EMC is a frontend-only ExC Shell SPA with no backend repo; all mutations and queries call external Adobe APIs (ESP, ESL) directly through a centralized ApiService with caching, validation, and dry-run support.
nodes.details: EMC (web-src/src/) is a React 18 + TypeScript + React Spectrum S2 SPA deployed via Adobe App Builder. There is no backend in this repo. All API calls route through services/api.ts (ApiService) and cachedApi wrapper: GET requests use 10s caching with request dedup and pattern-based invalidation; all mutations require input validation via validateString()/validateObject() before dispatch; all fetch calls pass through safeFetch() with ALLOWED_HOSTS validation. Two external backends: Adobe ESP (events/series/speakers endpoints) and ESL (lifecycle/venues/attendees). Auth uses Bearer token (IMS in prod, dev token locally) + x-gw-ims-org-id header. Dry-run mode available via apiService.enableDryRun(). Form state (EventForm, SeriesForm) persists to sessionStorage with debounced auto-save; multi-step FormWizard uses useEventFormComponent hook lifecycle (onGatherPayload, onAfterSave, onLoadResponse, validate) for step registration.

nodes.summary: Session form dirty-state tracking and unsaved-changes dialog: parent components receive `sessionHasOpenForm` prop to gate navigation; SessionForm detects dirty state and triggers callbacks; FormWizard integrates confirmation dialog before allowing navigation away.
nodes.details: The session management enhancement establishes a pattern for handling unsaved changes across the EventForm hierarchy. SessionManagementComponent tracks form state via `sessionHasOpenForm` prop and notifies parents of changes. SessionForm is responsible for detecting dirty state (form modifications) and invoking callbacks to signal this state upward. FormWizard consumes this signal and blocks navigation by rendering a confirmation dialog before allowing users to leave the form. This pattern ensures data loss prevention across nested form components without losing the ability to navigate intentionally. Apply this pattern to other multi-step forms in EMC that risk data loss on navigation.

nodes.summary: EMC centralizes all API calls through a singleton ApiService class with consistent error handling, authentication management, and mock-to-real API switching via config.json action URLs.
nodes.details: All external API calls route through ApiService.callAction<T>(actionName, params, method) in /web-src/src/services/api.ts. Authentication is set once via apiService.setAuthHeaders(token, org) and applied to all requests. Backend URLs are configured via apiService.setActionUrls(urls) from config.json, enabling mock-to-real switching without code changes: remove mock import, update the method to call this.callAction('actionName'), and add the URL to config.json actions object. Mock data lives in /web-src/src/mocks/ as TypeScript modules exporting both data and Promise-returning functions (with 300ms delay to simulate latency). This pattern decouples frontend from backend readiness and enables parallel development.

nodes.summary: EMC dev token system uses two-path bootstrap architecture: ExC Shell path (real IMS) vs. standalone path (dev token), with dev token activation gated by both hostname allowlist AND ?devtokenmode=true URL parameter.
nodes.details: The dev token system is never active in Experience Cloud Shell (bootstrapInExcShell() path); it only activates in standalone mode (bootstrapStandalone()) when both hostname is in DEV_TOKEN_ALLOWED_HOSTNAMES (localhost, 127.0.0.1, or specific adobeio-static.net subdomains) AND URL contains ?devtokenmode=true. The isDevTokenModeEnabled() function in web-src/src/config/env.ts enforces this dual gate. Dev token button visibility, token storage use in ApiService.getAuthToken(), and useDevToken hook all depend on this check. This ensures dev tokens never leak into production/staging deployments and cannot interfere with real IMS sessions in the shell.

nodes.summary: Production event publishing requires explicit user confirmation via AlertDialog before calling publishEvent; dev/stage builds skip this gate.
nodes.details: In EventForm.tsx, when ENVIRONMENT=prod, both handleComplete and executeSaveWithUrl paths funnel through requestPublishAfterUrlResolved, which opens a Spectrum 2 AlertDialog for user acceptance before invoking publishEvent. The extraPayload ref is cleared only on confirm or Cancel, not in onOpenChange, to preserve the payload if close handlers fire before onPrimaryAction executes. This pattern prevents accidental production event publication.

nodes.summary: Per-resource PUT payload sanitizers live in utils/dataFilters.ts and follow prepareEsp{Resource}PutPayload naming
nodes.details: Convention adopted across the EMC frontend: every ESP PUT endpoint has a corresponding prepareEsp{Resource}PutPayload function in web-src/src/utils/dataFilters.ts that calls filterSeriesData (or the resource-specific equivalent) in 'update' mode. This centralizes read-only-field stripping and ensures unpublish, archive, and external-update flows all go through the same validation layer. Do not invent ad-hoc filtering at the call site.

nodes.summary: EMC dark mode uses system prefers-color-scheme via usePreferredColorScheme hook, syncs React Spectrum 2 colorScheme prop, and defines semantic CSS tokens (--emc-field-*, --emc-event-form-shell-bg) that mirror compiled S2 Field colors (dark #111 fill, #444 border) under both @media and html[data-color-scheme] selectors for hydration safety.
nodes.details: The usePreferredColorScheme hook (web-src/src/hooks/usePreferredColorScheme.ts) subscribes to matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme: dark)') and sets document.documentElement.dataset.colorScheme, which is passed to S2Provider colorScheme prop in App/AuthGate/RBACGate. index.css defines light :root defaults and dark @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) overrides for both legacy --spectrum-global-* and new semantic tokens (--emc-field-bg, --emc-field-border, --emc-field-focus-ring). Tokens are duplicated under html[data-color-scheme='dark'] selector to ensure first paint and post-effect hydration alignment. Custom controls (Quill RTE via .rte-field-shell, Google Places venue field via .emc-field-like) suppress UA outline and use :focus-visible for keyboard focus rings while relying on border changes for mouse focus, matching S2 behavior. designSystem.ts SURFACES enum (shell/card/format-dialog) centralizes surface-level background tokens.

nodes.summary: Blocker encountered: RSVP API / EMC discrepancy (blocker)
nodes.details: Reported by cli-user: EMC has per-option RSVP UI state; event API only has rsvpFormFields visible/required.

nodes.summary: Parallel API queries for attendee status types are merged into a single result set; new status types require only type union updates and StatusBadge entries, not table/filter/export logic changes.
nodes.details: In EMC's Registrations page, attendee statuses (registered, waitlisted, declined) are fetched via parallel `?type=X` queries in `getAllEventAttendees()` (web-src/src/services/api.ts) and merged into a single `AttendeeStats` result. The `RegistrationStatus` type union (web-src/src/types/attendee.ts) controls which statuses exist. Adding a new status requires: (1) extending the `RegistrationStatus` union, (2) adding a `StatusBadge` variant entry (web-src/src/components/shared/StatusBadge.tsx), and (3) updating `AttendeeStats` interface. Table rendering, filtering, and CSV export are data-driven and automatically support new statuses without code changes.

nodes.summary: React Spectrum 2 Tabs component can crash when overflow/collapse unmounts its internal TabListStateContext; use SegmentedControl + conditional rendering instead.
nodes.details: S2 horizontal Tabs on the Registrations page (/registrations) can enter an overflow/collapse path that unmounts the react-aria-components Tabs shell, leaving TabListStateContext null and causing 'Cannot read properties of null (reading selectedKey)' crashes. Replace with SegmentedControl + SegmentedControlItem (the established EMC pattern) paired with selectedTab state to conditionally render the three sections (Registrations, Campaigns, Sessions). This avoids the context unmounting issue entirely. See web-src/src/pages/Registrations/Registrations.tsx for the applied pattern.

nodes.summary: EMC migrated from sidebar to top navigation (gnav) layout; TopNav component in SideBar.tsx with UserPanel compact mode; App.tsx grid changed from ['sidebar', 'content'] to ['header', 'content'] with rows ['auto', '1fr'].
nodes.details: The layout shift encodes a durable architectural pattern: (1) SideBar.tsx was repurposed as TopNav with horizontal nav items and brand logo on left, user panel on right; (2) UserPanel.tsx gained a `compact` prop that hides email/org and reduces avatar size for header context; (3) App.tsx grid layout changed from 2-column sidebar model to 2-row header model with grid areas ['header', 'content'] and rows ['auto', '1fr']; (4) Navigation links use `.nav-link` class with bottom border (3px solid transparent) for active state, not background highlight; (5) Content area must have `gridArea='content'` and overflow scroll enabled. This pattern is reusable for any future layout refactors and clarifies the component responsibility split.

nodes.summary: POI (point of interest) must not be auto-hydrated into event objects for SharePoint push; responsibility lies with event marketers and FE validation.

This was reverted because: (1) event marketers are responsible for consciously excluding POI from form field selections during event creation, and (2) the EMC console FE (owned by Qiyun) provides safeguarding at RSVP field selection, where POI option visibility is already controlled. Do not auto-inject POI into the event hydration pipeline; enforce the contract that POI inclusion is an explicit, user-driven choice at form design time.

nodes.summary: IMS user context must be threaded as a prop through component tree (App → UserPanel, SideBar); UserPanel displays profile data with graceful fallback when IMS profile unavailable.
nodes.details: The UserPanel component receives an `ims` prop containing `{ profile?: IMSProfile, org?: string, token?: string }` where IMSProfile has `userId`, `name`, `email`. Components extract user context via optional chaining (e.g., `ims.profile?.name || 'Guest'`). When `ims.profile` is absent, UserPanel renders 'Not Connected' state. This pattern establishes the contract for how IMS data flows through the EMC frontend: App.tsx passes `ims` to both UserPanel and SideBar, and any component needing user context receives the same IMS object structure. Token is never rendered; user ID is truncated in UI for privacy.

nodes.summary: CSV export filename convention: prefix with event title and ISO datetime, sanitize user input, append .csv extension only at download time.
nodes.details: EMC attendee and campaign exports use a standardized filename pattern: `[event-title]_[YYYY-MM-DD_HH-MM-SS]` for attendees, `[event-title]_campaigns_[YYYY-MM-DD_HH-MM-SS]` for campaigns. The `utils/csvExport.ts` module provides `sanitizeFilename()` and `exportDatetime()` helpers to enforce this. This pattern applies across ExportDialog.tsx (attendee) and CampaignExportDialog (campaign tab).

nodes.summary: EMC's per-option RSVP UI state model does not map cleanly to the event API's flat rsvpFormFields structure
nodes.details: The Event Management Console maintains granular per-option UI state for RSVP fields, while the underlying event API only exposes coarser visible/required flags on rsvpFormFields. This impedance mismatch requires a translation layer or dual-source loading strategy on the frontend. Future pods touching RSVP field configuration should budget time to handle this gap explicitly rather than assuming API parity.

nodes.summary: RSVP field metadata is loaded from external event-libs config via configService.getRsvpConfig; boolean attendee fields render as 'Yes'/'No' in UI and CSV exports.
nodes.details: RegistrationFieldsComponent loads RSVP field catalogs via configService.getRsvpConfig (with caching/retry), and renders each field's Label from the JSON config. In AttendeeTableComponent, boolean columns (e.g., requiresSxswTicket) display as 'yes'/'no' in table cells; AttendeeFiltersComponent maps filter chips to 'Yes'/'No'; ExportDialog normalizes boolean columns to 'Yes'/'No' in CSV. The field definition lives in external event-libs experiencecloud.json (not in EMC repo), following the Type/Options conventions of other Experience Cloud RSVP fields. Add requiresSxswTicket?: boolean to attendee.ts type definitions.

nodes.summary: Do not omit detailPagePath from event PUT payloads; instead, use dataFilters to toggle submittable: true when title changes, coordinating with backend OpenAPI spec updates.
nodes.details: When updating an event via ESL PUT, detailPagePath was previously omitted because the backend marked it read-only. However, title changes require a new detailPagePath (new DA page). The fix: in useEventFormSave.ts, call dataFilters to set detailPagePath.submittable = true before the PUT, and detect title changes to trigger the DA page path dialog. This requires coordinated backend changes to the OpenAPI spec to allow the field in PUT requests. The anti-pattern is assuming a read-only field can never be submitted; instead, use conditional submittability flags in dataFilters based on business logic (e.g., title mutation).

nodes.summary: When hydrating event payloads from DynamoDB kinesis records with sk=localizations, source seriesId and detailPagePath from the pre-fetched liveData object, not from newData.itemData (which lacks these fields).
nodes.details: In EventDataStreamProcessor.js, when processing a localization record change (sk=localizations), the newData.itemData payload contains only localizations and localizationOverrides. To build a complete hydrated event for ESL, pull seriesId and detailPagePath from liveData (fetched via eventService.getEventData at processRecord start), not from newData.itemData. This is safe because EventService.updateVenue writes the new detailPagePath to DynamoDB before the venue record fires the kinesis stream, ensuring liveData.detailPagePath is current. Omitting these fields causes DA webhook page creation to fail or write to wrong locations.

nodes.summary: Orphaned page cleanup is triggered synchronously at Kinesis record-processing time by detecting detailPagePath changes via event history, not deferred to the handler loop.
nodes.details: When a published, liveUpdate event is modified, EventDataStreamProcessor calls EventService.getEventHistory(eventId) to fetch the event's prior states. findLastPublishedHistory walks the history array newest-to-oldest, skipping entries whose timestamp matches the current modificationTime (race-condition guard), and returns the first entry with published=true && liveUpdate=true. If that entry's detailPagePath differs from the current one, sendEventDataToWebhook is called immediately with isDeleteEvent=true and the old path, allowing downstream consumers (e.g. SharePoint) to clean up orphaned pages without waiting for the main handler. History fetch failures are caught and logged; processing continues normally (no Kinesis retry). Timestamp comparison uses String() coercion on both sides to handle type differences between DynamoDB-unmarshalled numbers and history API values.

nodes.summary: Do not use Kinesis payload as source of truth for event metadata; always rehydrate from DynamoDB on every stream record, even for localization-only updates.
nodes.details: EMC emits two Kinesis records per event save (one for event, one for localization), but only the first carries full metadata (e.g., cloud-type). In EventDataStreamProcessor.js processRecord(), the prior logic conditionally rehydrated from DynamoDB only when liveUpdate=true, causing localization records to forward partial payloads downstream. This broke `.page` preview RSVP forms when the second (partial) write overwrote the first (complete) write. Fix: always rebuild newData.itemData from liveData (DynamoDB), falling back to Kinesis payload only for localizations and localizationOverrides fields. This ensures both eventData and localization Kinesis records produce fully hydrated payloads to Hoolihan/AIO DA.

nodes.summary: ESP resources use modificationTime for optimistic concurrency on PUT; clients must round-trip it
nodes.details: Every ESP PUT on an updatable resource (event, series, session, speaker) requires the modificationTime field to match the server's last-known value. If they differ, PUT returns 409 with the current server state. Clients must therefore: (a) capture modificationTime on every GET, (b) send it back unchanged on the next PUT, (c) re-fetch on 409 and merge. Dropping or recomputing modificationTime client-side is the most common cause of silent edit failures on EMC.

nodes.summary: EMC caching and throttling utilities follow a three-layer request pattern (cache → pending → new request) with function-name-based key generation, 10-second default TTL, pattern-based invalidation, and automatic cache busting on mutations.

Cache can be inspected via `getCacheStats()` and cleared via `clearCache()` or `invalidateCache(pattern)`.

This pattern establishes the contract for how IMS data flows through the EMC frontend: App.tsx passes `ims` to both UserPanel and SideBar, and any component needing user context receives the same IMS object structure. Token is never rendered; user ID is truncated in UI for privacy.

nodes.summary: Claude agent access policy: read-only commands auto-approved, destructive operations require explicit approval; word-boundary matching prevents false positives in command filtering.
nodes.details: The EMC repo grants Claude agent file-edit permissions without prompting (defaultMode: acceptEdits) but enforces approval gates on destructive operations. Allowed commands (ls, cat, grep, find, echo, pwd, which) use word-boundary matching in Bash regex — e.g., Bash(ls *) matches 'ls -la' but not 'lsof', preventing accidental approval of unintended commands. Denied list includes rm -rf *, git push *, git reset --hard *, git merge *, and any --force flags. This pattern balances agent velocity (no friction on safe reads/edits) against repository safety (human-in-loop for irreversible changes).

nodes.summary: Speakers and sponsors are grouped by role/tier with per-group drag-and-drop reordering; role/tier changes move items to the end of the new group and trigger per-group ordinal recomputation.

nodes.summary: Silent failures in Splash attendee status updates (PUT /external/events/:id/attendees/:id) due to missing externalAttendeeId → attendeeId mappings caused EMC/Splash count mismatches; resolved via direct DynamoDB correction.

nodes.summary: Manager classes in events-service-platform automatically persist request body fields via spread operator; schema changes alone are sufficient for new optional fields without code changes.

nodes.summary: Event attendee route handlers use explicit field mappings instead of spreading req.body, causing OpenAPI-validated fields to silently drop before persistence.

nodes.summary: Do not omit detailPagePath from event PUT payloads; instead, use dataFilters to toggle submittable: true when title changes, coordinating with backend OpenAPI spec updates.

nodes.summary: ESL must mirror ESP's AttendeeTextField relaxations (maxLength 100→200, newline-tolerant regex) to avoid being a stricter validation gate than upstream, preventing legacy attendee data from passing re-validation.

Authentication is set once via apiService.setAuthHeaders(token, org) and applied to all requests. Backend URLs are configured via apiService.setActionUrls(urls) from config.json, enabling mock-to-real switching without code changes: remove mock import, update the method to call this.callAction('actionName'), and add the URL to config.json actions object. Mock data lives in /web-src/src/mocks/ as TypeScript modules exporting both data and Promise-returning functions (with 300ms delay to simulate latency). This pattern decouples frontend from backend readiness and enables parallel development.

nodes.summary: Attendees resource has dual CRUD surfaces: standalone /v1/attendees/* for lifecycle management, and nested /v1/events/:eventId/attendees/* for event-specific membership operations only.
nodes.details: The attendees CRUD operations split across two route hierarchies: /v1/attendees/{create,read,update,delete}.js handle attendee entity lifecycle (create new attendee, read attendee details, update attendee profile, delete attendee). The nested /v1/events/:eventId/attendees/* routes (in src/routes/events/attendees/) handle only event membership: POST adds an *existing* attendee to an event (does not create attendees), GET lists attendees for an event, DELETE removes attendee from event, PUT updates attendee's event-specific state. This separation prevents attendee creation from being coupled to event enrollment. Enforce via attendeesMgr.js and eventsMgr.js: standalone routes call attendeesMgr directly; nested routes validate attendee exists before calling eventsMgr membership methods.

nodes.summary: Campaign-aware RSVP registration: when campaignId URL param is present, fetch campaign capacity and apply waitlist rules before attendee creation.

If present and event is not full, call getCampaign(eventId, campaignId) to fetch campaign capacity (attendeeLimit, attendeeCount, waitlistAttendeeCount). Apply waitlist logic: if attendeeLimit === attendeeCount, mark waitlisted; if attendeeLimit > attendeeCount and waitlistAttendeeCount > 0, mark waitlisted; if attendeeLimit > attendeeCount and waitlistAttendeeCount === 0, register normally. If no attendeeLimit, pass campaignId without campaign logic. Skip campaign lookup when event is already full. campaignId is sanitized in events-form.js (regex ^[\w-]{1,128}$) and added to EVENT_ATTENDEE_DATA_FILTER in data-utils.js so it flows into the event attendee API body.

nodes.summary: Event Form uses 4-step wizard structure where Step 1 groups 5 logical components (format, tags, info, dates, venue) rather than separating into individual steps; this matches v1 reference and improves UX.
nodes.details: The EventForm wizard in EMC follows a deliberate 4-step structure (not 8) where Step 1 contains EventFormatComponent, Tags, Event Info, Date/Time, and Venue components as logical sub-sections. This pattern groups related fields (e.g., all basic event metadata in Step 1) while keeping the overall flow concise. Step 2 handles Speakers/Hosts, Step 3 handles images, Step 4 handles RSVP/status. When implementing new event forms or extending this wizard, maintain this grouping: do not split Step 1 into separate steps unless UX research shows users abandon multi-step forms at >6 steps. The FormWizard shared component manages progress tracking and navigation across all steps.

nodes.summary: EMC frontend organizes event form as 13 modular components under EventForm/ directory, each owning a logical section (venue, speakers, agenda, etc.), composed by EventForm.tsx wizard container.
nodes.details: The EventForm/ directory contains 13 specialized components (EventFormatComponent, EventInfoComponent, VenueComponent, SpeakersComponent, SponsorsComponent, AgendaComponent, EventImagesComponent, ProfilesComponent, RegistrationConfigComponent, RegistrationFieldsComponent, PageMetadataComponent, plus index.ts barrel export) that are composed into a multi-step wizard by the parent EventForm.tsx container. Each component owns a logical domain (e.g., VenueComponent handles Google Places integration, SpeakersComponent manages speaker CRUD, RegistrationFieldsComponent configures RSVP form fields). This modular decomposition enables independent testing, reuse, and maintenance of form sections. The barrel export (index.ts) centralizes imports for the parent wizard.

nodes.summary: Production event publishing requires explicit user confirmation via AlertDialog before calling publishEvent; dev/stage builds skip this gate.
nodes.details: In EventForm.tsx, when ENVIRONMENT=prod, both handleComplete and executeSaveWithUrl paths funnel through requestPublishAfterUrlResolved, which opens a Spectrum 2 AlertDialog for user acceptance before invoking publishEvent. The extraPayload ref is cleared only on confirm or Cancel, not in onOpenChange, to preserve the payload if close handlers fire before onPrimaryAction executes. This pattern prevents accidental production event publication.

nodes.summary: Session form dirty-state tracking and unsaved-changes dialog: parent components receive `sessionHasOpenForm` prop to gate navigation; SessionForm detects dirty state and triggers callbacks; FormWizard integrates confirmation dialog before allowing navigation away.
nodes.details: The session management enhancement establishes a pattern for handling unsaved changes across the EventForm hierarchy. SessionManagementComponent tracks form state via `sessionHasOpenForm` prop and notifies parents of changes. SessionForm is responsible for detecting dirty state (form modifications) and invoking callbacks to signal this state upward. FormWizard consumes this signal and blocks navigation by rendering a confirmation dialog before allowing users to leave the form. This pattern ensures data loss prevention across nested form components without losing the ability to navigate intentionally. Apply this pattern to other multi-step forms in EMC that risk data loss on navigation.

nodes.summary: Orphaned page cleanup is triggered synchronously at Kinesis record-processing time by detecting detailPagePath changes via event history, not deferred to the handler loop.
nodes.details: When a published, liveUpdate event is modified, EventDataStreamProcessor calls EventService.getEventHistory(eventId) to fetch the event's prior states. findLastPublishedHistory walks the history array newest-to-oldest, skipping entries whose timestamp matches the current modificationTime (race-condition guard), and returns the first entry with published=true && liveUpdate=true. If that entry's detailPagePath differs from the current one, sendEventDataToWebhook is called immediately with isDeleteEvent=true and the old path, allowing downstream consumers (e.g. SharePoint) to clean up orphaned pages without waiting for the main handler. History fetch failures are caught and logged; processing continues normally (no Kinesis retry). Timestamp comparison uses String() coercion on both sides to handle type differences between DynamoDB-unmarshalled numbers and history API values.

nodes.summary: Invite-only events gate RSVP behind `inviteOnly` flag and campaign URL param; replace button with text message rather than disable.
nodes.details: The invite-only RSVP feature gates registration on two conditions: (1) an `inviteOnly` event flag from the backend, and (2) a campaign URL parameter. When both conditions are met, the RSVP button is replaced with a text message instead of being disabled. This pattern prevents accidental user confusion and clarifies that the event is not available for self-service registration. Check `event-libs/v1/blocks/events-form/events-form.js` for the gating logic and button replacement implementation.

nodes.summary: Response validation must be permissive for legacy attendee data; request-side validation is decoupled and handled separately by RSVP forms.
nodes.details: PhoneNumber and AttendeeTextField schemas in GET /v1/events/{eventId}/attendees responses were over-constrained (pattern: ^\+?[0-9]+$, maxLength: 20 for phone; pattern rejecting all HTML for text fields with maxLength: 100), causing 12.8% of production attendee records to fail HTTP 418 validation. The fix relaxes response schemas (PhoneNumber: drop pattern, maxLength 30; AttendeeTextField: newline-tolerant pattern ^(?![\s\S]*<[^>]*>)[\s\S]*$, maxLength 200) while explicitly documenting that form-side input validation remains the responsibility of RSVP-form frontends. This resolves the architectural tension: the service layer must accept and return legacy data as-is; sanitization and strict validation belong upstream.

nodes.summary: RSVP button state machine: six mutually-exclusive states (loading, default, registered, waitlisted, to-waitlist, event-closed) driven by authentication, capacity, and registration status; text and accessibility managed via dictionary keys and tabindex.
nodes.details: RSVP buttons in event-libs use hash patterns (#rsvp-form, #webinar-marketo-form) to trigger decorateEvent processing. State transitions are: Loading (disabled, tabindex=-1) → Default (enabled) → one of {Registered, Waitlisted, To Waitlist, Event Closed} based on user auth (allow-guest-registration meta), event capacity (ESP API), and waitlist config (allow-wait-listing meta). Each state maps to a dictionary key (rsvp-loading-cta-text, registered-cta-text, waitlist-cta-text, event-full-cta-text, etc.). Form 400 errors distinguish event-full vs campaign-full (via ?campaign URL param) and whether waitlisting is enabled, using separate error keys (event-full-error-msg, campaign-full-no-waitlist-error-msg, etc.). Custom button text uses pipe separator (text|fallback). State updates are reactive via BlockMediator subscriptions.

nodes.summary: Attendee status endpoint exposes only registration state, not full attendee record or event details.
nodes.details: The GET /v1/events/{eventId}/attendees/{attendeeId or me}/status endpoint returns a minimal payload with only the `registered` boolean field. This establishes that status queries are scoped to registration state alone, not full attendee metadata or event context. The endpoint supports both explicit attendeeId and 'me' (current user) path parameters. Future status-related queries should follow this minimal-payload pattern rather than returning full attendee objects.

nodes.summary: Image updates in Kinesis stream lack eventId in payload; extract from DynamoDB partition key instead of relying on newData field.
nodes.details: When images are updated via the Kinesis event stream (EventDataStreamProcessor.js), the newData object does not contain an eventId field, unlike event object updates. To correlate image records with their parent event, extract eventId from the DynamoDB partition key: `event.eventId = keys.pk.split('#').pop()`. Without this extraction, image updates fail to propagate to the event record until the event itself is modified. This pattern applies to all image-related Kinesis processing in the events-kinesis-processor Lambda.

nodes.summary: ESP event-speaker PUT body contract is { speakerId, speakerType, ordinal, creationTime, modificationTime } and nothing else
nodes.details: Per ESP OpenAPI, /v1/events/:eventId/speakers/:speakerId PUT accepts only those five fields. Echoing the full GET response (spreading dependentData) fails server-side validation and has been the root cause of repeated 400s on edit. When using callWithDependency's body-builder, fall back to dependentData per-field: body.X ?? dependentData.X. creationTime and modificationTime are server-issued; do not let callers override them. The same pattern applies to all ESP PUTs on speaker resources.

nodes.summary: Do not rely on hashchange events to open modals when the target hash is already present in the URL; force a re-trigger by clearing and re-setting the hash.
nodes.details: In event-libs/v1/blocks/chrono-box/chrono-box.js, clicking an RSVP link when the URL hash already matches the modal target will not fire a hashchange event, preventing Milo's modal listener from triggering. The fix: clear the hash, then re-set it to the target value to force the event. Guard against double-triggering by checking if the modal is already rendered before re-setting the hash. This pattern applies to any Milo modal integration where the same hash may be clicked multiple times in a session.

nodes.summary: Scope configs (rsvp, locales, customAttributes) are the authoritative source for event metadata; publishing profiles are deprecated but retained for backward compatibility during migration.
nodes.details: Events created under Creative Events (25f26faa-f8e2-4e99-b341-81a3995ef9af) and Enterprise Events (d758a3bc-ff31-4bfe-a2f5-343f074aec6c) scopes must define four config types: rsvp (pool of form fields), locales (localeNames, localeUrlCodes), and customAttributes (with primaryProductName and promotionalItems attributes). The Kinesis processor (events-kinesis-processor/ServiceProcessor.applyRelatedData) must call GET /v1/events/{eventId}/configs to hydrate event.locales, event.customAttributesConfig, and event.rsvpConfig at stream-processing time; event DDB records store only user selections (rsvpFormFields, customAttributes[] with valueId), not full definitions. Publishing profiles remain in the payload for backward compat but are no longer the source of truth. hoolihan-webhooks must read primary product from event.customAttributes[] where attribute='primaryProductName', promotional items from customAttributes[] where attribute='promotionalItems', RSVP pool from event.rsvpConfig.rsvpFormFields[], and locales from event.locales.localeNames/localeUrlCodes.

nodes.summary: Invite-only events require a valid campaign URL parameter (?campaign=) to enable RSVP; gating occurs at button-disable and form-build stages with dictionary-driven error messaging.
nodes.details: When an event has inviteOnly=true, RSVP is blocked unless a valid campaign ID is present in the URL query string. Validation uses getValidCampaignIdFromUrl() (utils/utils.js) against CAMPAIGN_ID_PATTERN (utils/constants.js). Gating is enforced in two places: (1) updateRSVPButtonState in decorate.js disables the button early via setCtaState('inviteOnlyNoCampaign'), and (2) events-form.js handleProfile blocks form construction entirely and renders an error message keyed to rsvp-invite-only-no-campaign-cta-text in the dictionary. The campaign ID is then passed to submitForm for server-side validation.

nodes.summary: RSVP button and form 400-error handling must respect campaign capacity when ?campaign URL param is present and valid, falling back to event capacity otherwise, with campaign-specific error messages and UI state.
nodes.details: When a valid campaign ID is present in the URL (?campaign=...), use getCampaign() to fetch campaign capacity and apply it to both RSVP button state (updateRSVPButtonState in decorate.js) and form 400-error handling (buildErrorMsg and submit handler in events-form.js). If campaign fetch fails or campaign ID is invalid (validate via CAMPAIGN_ID_PATTERN in constances.js), fall back to event capacity. On 400 response with campaign present, use campaign-full-error-msg or campaign-full-no-waitlist-error-msg keys and update submit button to waitlist or event-full state (disabled if no waitlist) to keep copy and UI consistent. This ensures campaign-level capacity gates take precedence over event-level gates when applicable.

nodes.summary: Event speaker PUT request body must be contract-shaped; do not spread raw GET response into PUT payload.
nodes.details: The API service layer enforces a specific payload shape for speaker PUT operations (web-src/src/services/api.ts). When updating event speakers, construct the request body to match the server's expected contract rather than spreading the GET response directly. This prevents field mismatches and validation failures. See Sessions and EventForm components for correct usage patterns.

nodes.summary: Do not spread GET response into PUT body; construct narrow association payloads with only required fields plus timestamps.
nodes.details: In `web-src/src/services/api.ts`, `updateSpeakerInEvent` previously merged the full GET response (minus `creationTime`) into the PUT body, sending unintended fields to ESP. nodes.summary: Speakers and sponsors are grouped by role/tier with per-group drag-and-drop reordering; role/tier changes move items to the end of the new group and trigger per-group ordinal recomputation.
nodes.details: In SpeakersComponent.tsx and SponsorsComponent.tsx, items are grouped by speakerType and tier respectively. Drag-and-drop is restricted to within-group moves only (cross-group drops are blocked). When a speaker's role or sponsor's tier is changed via inline picker, the item is moved to the end of the new group. On save, onAfterSave computes per-group ordinals for both components. SponsorData now includes an optional ordinal field, and updateSponsorInEvent in api.ts explicitly preserves ordinal in the merge logic. Both components display a disclaimer note that group display order on the DA page is governed by template configuration, not EMC form ordering.

nodes.summary: Event speaker PUT request body must be contract-shaped; do not spread raw GET response into PUT payload.
nodes.details: The API service layer enforces a specific payload shape for speaker PUT operations (web-src/src/services/api.ts). When updating event speakers, construct the request body to match the server's expected contract rather than spreading the GET response directly. This prevents field mismatches and validation failures. See Sessions and EventForm components for correct usage patterns.

nodes.summary: Sessions Hub text search is scoped to title, speaker names, and tag labels; descriptions excluded by default unless `search-include-description` block class is set.
nodes.details: The filterSessions function in event-libs/v1/blocks/sessions-hub/sessions-hub.js implements a three-field search pattern: title, speaker (first/last/full-name substring), and tag labels are matched case-insensitively against trimmed queries ≥2 characters. Session descriptions are intentionally excluded from the default search scope to reduce noise; marketers can opt into description matching by adding the `search-include-description` block class. A query of 1 character or whitespace-only does not filter by text, leaving all sessions visible subject to tab/tag filters. When a qualifying search returns zero results, the no-results UI (role="status", aria-live="polite") is shown and the session grid is hidden.

nodes.summary: Do not omit server modification time (mtime) when updating session-time API without page refresh; failure to persist and send mtime in consecutive calls triggers OptimisticLockExceptionError.
nodes.details: The session-time API endpoint requires the server's modification timestamp (mtime) to be stored after each response and included in subsequent PUT/PATCH requests. When session-time params are updated in-memory without a page refresh, the mtime must be extracted from the server response and cached in component state (e.g., Sessions.tsx) so it is available for the next API call. Omitting mtime causes the server to reject the update as a stale write. Additionally, ensure POST is only called once during session creation; subsequent updates must use PUT/PATCH with the cached mtime to avoid duplicate session-time records.

nodes.summary: Session registration UI follows a three-state model (Registered/Waitlisted, Able to Register, Blocked) with explicit predicates for each state; SessionTimeFull responses must be read from body, not just HTTP status.
nodes.details: In `event-libs/v1/blocks/sessions-hub/sessions-hub.js`, the per-card CTA must implement exactly three states: (1) Registered/Waitlisted badge (blue, shows checkmark + text from `waitlist-cta-text` dictionary key, hover swaps to unregister action), (2) Able-to-register button (direct `registerForSessionTime` API call, no modal), (3) Blocked button (disabled `.sh-btn-blocked`, labeled from `Registration unavailable` dictionary key). Use the pure predicate `isSessionRegistrationBlocked({ isEventWaitlisted, isEventClosed, inviteOnlyBlocked })` to determine blocked state. For session-time registration responses, read `resp.body.data.registrationStatus === 'waitlisted'` to distinguish waitlist from full registration (2xx with waitlist status must set `session.isWaitlisted`, not `isRegistered`). Use `isSessionTimeFullError(resp)` helper to detect SessionTimeFull errors by checking `error.code | errorCode | error | type | message` fields defensively. Event-level waitlist state (`rsvpData.registrationStatus === 'waitlisted'`) blocks all per-card registration; event-closed state (computed from `isFull && !allowWaitlisting`, accepting both boolean and string `'true'`) also blocks. Banner visibility: keep visible for waitlisted users (only hide when `isEventRegistered === true`), render `sh-banner-waitlist-msg` paragraph with `getEventWaitlistBannerMessage(manager, { eventTitle })` helper from `dictionary-manager.js`.

nodes.summary: Attendee string fields are validated via reusable OpenAPI schemas (NoTagsString, AttendeeName, AttendeeTextField, SpecialRequirements, PhoneNumber) enforced by express-openapi-validator at the API layer to prevent injection attacks and enforce length limits.
nodes.details: All attendee string inputs must pass schema validation in src/api/openapi.json before reaching business logic. NoTagsString rejects values containing `<…>` (HTML/script tags). AttendeeName (firstName, lastName) max 30 chars; AttendeeTextField (companyName, countryRegion, organizationName, title, dietaryRestrictions, etc.) max 100 chars; SpecialRequirements max 1000 chars; PhoneNumber (mobilePhone, businessPhone) digits + `+` only, max 20 chars. Website (format: uri) and executiveAssistantEmail (format: email) use existing OpenAPI format constraints; contactMethod uses enum. Validation is declarative in openapi.json and enforced by express-openapi-validator middleware — do not add runtime validation in handlers.

nodes.summary: Do not explicitly remove() nodes that remain within the chrono-box host during reparenting; rely on innerHTML clearing for in-host reorders to avoid redundant teardown.
nodes.details: chrono-box reparent cleanup must distinguish between nodes moved outside the host (which require explicit remove()) and nodes reordered within the subtree (which will be cleared by the next innerHTML swap). Guard orphan removal with `!chronoBoxEl.contains(node) && node.isConnected` in cleanupChronoBoxOutboundNodes. Calling remove() on in-host nodes triggers unnecessary teardown and diverges from the single-shot slot-clearing behavior. See event-libs/v1/blocks/chrono-box/chrono-box.js and corresponding unit test for the guard pattern.

nodes.summary: Do not rely on :focus:not(:focus-visible) CSS to suppress focus rings when Milo's getModal uses .focus({ focusVisible: true }) — the flag forces :focus-visible to match regardless of input method.
nodes.details: Milo's getModal helper focuses the first FOCUSABLE element using .focus({ focusVisible: true }), which explicitly forces :focus-visible to match even on programmatic focus. CSS rules like :focus:not(:focus-visible) cannot suppress this ring. Instead, ensure the first FOCUSABLE in modal DOM order is an element where outline: none is already applied (e.g., a heading with tabindex="0"), or add outline: none to the element that will receive initial focus. In profile-cards/profile-cards.js, the fix was to add tabindex="0" to the card-name h2 in buildModalContent so it precedes social links in focus order, and the existing .card-name:focus { outline: none; } rule suppresses the ring.

nodes.summary: ESP event-speaker PUT body contract is { speakerId, speakerType, ordinal, creationTime, modificationTime } and nothing else
