The same pattern applies to all ESP PUTs on speaker resources.

nodes.summary: Event attendee route handlers use explicit field mappings instead of spreading req.body, causing OpenAPI-validated fields to silently drop before persistence.
nodes.details: The attendee CRUD routes (create.js, update.js, read.js) in src/routes/events/attendees/ build eventAttendee objects by hand-picking fields rather than spreading req.body. This means fields validated by the OpenAPI spec (e.g., requiresTicket) can pass validation but never reach DynamoDB or the response. When adding a new attendee field, it must be explicitly added to all three route handlers' field mappings, or it will be silently dropped. Use explicit field mappings only when you need to exclude or transform fields; otherwise, spread req.body and filter at the schema layer.

nodes.summary: RSVP contactMethods field must not be spread directly from GET response into PUT payload; use prepareContactMethodsForPut helper to normalize shape.
nodes.details: The events-form block's RSVP submission was spreading the GET response contactMethods array directly into the PUT body, causing server-side validation failures when field shapes diverged between read and write contracts. The fix introduces a normalization step (prepareContactMethodsForPut in event-libs/v1/blocks/events-form/events-form.js) that maps the GET schema to the PUT schema before submission. This pattern applies to all ESP PUT operations: never assume GET and PUT payloads have identical field structures; always use a prepare* helper to bridge the contract gap.

nodes.summary: Spreading a GET response back into an ESP PUT body trips readOnly.openapi.validation
nodes.details: ESP marks several fields as read-only on PUT (e.g. targetCms on /v1/series/:id). Series unpublish / archive / external-update flows previously echoed the full GET response into the PUT body, which fails ESP's OpenAPI validator with readOnly.openapi.validation. Fix: always filter the payload through the resource-specific prepareEsp*PutPayload helper before PUT. For series use prepareEspSeriesPutPayload (wraps filterSeriesData in 'update' mode). For events use prepareEslEventPutPayload. New ESP PUT endpoints should add a sibling helper in utils/dataFilters.ts before the call site is added.

nodes.summary: Silent failures in Splash attendee status updates (PUT /external/events/:id/attendees/:id) due to missing externalAttendeeId → attendeeId mappings caused EMC/Splash count mismatches; resolved via direct DynamoDB correction.
nodes.details: When Splash sends status updates via PUT /external/events/:id/attendees/:id without a valid externalAttendeeId → attendeeId mapping in the service layer, the request fails silently rather than returning an error, leaving EMC counts stale while Splash reflects the true state. This caused deltas of 135+ waitlisted and 80+ declined records. Future agents should: (1) audit the attendee mapping lookup logic in the PUT handler to ensure it returns explicit errors on missing mappings rather than silently skipping updates, (2) add monitoring/alerting on PUT /external/events/:id/attendees/:id response codes to catch similar silent failures early, (3) recognize that zzTest migration scripts in this repo are the canonical runbook for data reconciliation when such mismatches occur.

nodes.summary: ESP OpenAPI spec must define response schemas for all HTTP status codes returned by endpoints, including 200; missing schemas cause runtime validation failures.
nodes.details: The events-service-platform validates responses against the OpenAPI spec at runtime. If an endpoint returns a 200 status code but the spec lacks a schema definition for that code, the request fails with 'no schema defined for status code' error. This applies to POST /v1/events/{eventId}/attendees and all other endpoints. Always add response schema definitions (including status code, content-type, and body shape) to src/api/openapi.json when adding or modifying endpoints, even for success cases.

nodes.summary: Do not replace entire itemData objects in DynamoDB PUT operations without preserving required fields; use merge/patch semantics or enforce all required fields in the request schema.
nodes.details: Publishing profiles were created with status: 'active', but PUT /v1/publishing-profiles/{profileId} requests that omitted status would replace the entire stored itemData, removing the field. This caused later GET /v1/events/{eventId}/publishing-profiles responses to fail OpenAPI validation (418 error) because status is a required field on PublishingProfile schema. Fix: (1) add defensive fallback in profile read paths to return status: 'active' if missing, (2) make status required on PublishingProfileUpdateRequest schema to prevent future drops, (3) ensure PublishingProfile response schema enforces status as required. This pattern applies to all DynamoDB-backed resources where PUT replaces rather than merges.

nodes.summary: Events Kinesis processor must send fully hydrated payloads (including speaker, sponsor, venue details) to AIO DA webhook on all create/update operations, not just event-data modifications.
nodes.details: The EventDataStreamProcessor Lambda was sending non-hydrated payloads to the AIO DA webhook when updates occurred only in speaker, sponsor, or venue entities, rather than in the event data itself. The fix ensures that all payloads sent to the DA webhook include complete hydration of related entities (speaker, sponsor, venue details) regardless of which entity triggered the update. This is a contract requirement: DA webhook consumers expect fully hydrated payloads on every create/update event, not partial payloads. See EventDataStreamProcessor.js and related test files (processRecord.test.js) for the hydration logic.

nodes.summary: Localization Kinesis records omit non-localization fields like rsvpFormFields; always fetch the full event record before scope filtering when hydrating from a localization change.
nodes.details: In ServiceProcessor.js, when a localization record change triggers `callHydratedEvent` with `forceSpWrite=true`, the hydrated payload lacks `rsvpFormFields` because Kinesis localization records only carry localization-scoped fields. The full event record (sk: event) must be fetched via `eventService.getEventData()` before scope config filtering runs, otherwise `rsvpConfig.rsvpFormFields` will be empty. Check for `forceSpWrite && !rsvpFormFields` to gate this parallel fetch and avoid redundant calls on non-localization event modifications.

nodes.summary: Per-resource PUT payload sanitizers live in utils/dataFilters.ts and follow prepareEsp{Resource}PutPayload naming
nodes.details: Convention adopted across the EMC frontend: every ESP PUT endpoint has a corresponding prepareEsp{Resource}PutPayload function in web-src/src/utils/dataFilters.ts that calls filterSeriesData (or the resource-specific equivalent) in 'update' mode. This centralizes read-only-field stripping and ensures unpublish, archive, and external-update flows all go through the same validation layer. Do not invent ad-hoc filtering at the call site.

nodes.summary: Do not spread GET response objects directly into ESP series PUT bodies; omit read-only fields like targetCms using prepareEspSeriesPutPayload.
nodes.details: ESP enforces read-only constraints on series PUT endpoints (updateSeriesExternal, publishSeries, unpublishSeries, archiveSeries). The Series Dashboard receives full series objects from GET /series/{id}, which include targetCms. Callers must filter these via prepareEspSeriesPutPayload (in web-src/src/utils/dataFilters.ts) before PUT, which wraps filterSeriesData(..., 'update') to drop non-updatable fields. POST (createSeriesExternal) does not apply this filter—targetCms is allowed on create. This pattern prevents readOnly.openapi.validation errors and ensures consistency across all series mutation helpers.

nodes.details: ESP marks several fields as read-only on PUT (e.g. targetCms on /v1/series/:id). nodes.summary: ESP resources use modificationTime for optimistic concurrency on PUT; clients must round-trip it
nodes.details: Every ESP PUT on an updatable resource (event, series, session, speaker) requires the modificationTime field to match the server's last-known value. If they differ, PUT returns 409 with the current server state. Clients must therefore: (a) capture modificationTime on every GET, (b) send it back unchanged on the next PUT, (c) re-fetch on 409 and merge. Dropping or recomputing modificationTime client-side is the most common cause of silent edit failures on EMC.

nodes.summary: Session-time helpers must return SessionTimeInfo so React state can update without a page refresh
nodes.details: createSessionTimeForSession and upsertSessionTimeForSession previously returned Promise<void>, which dropped the API's sessionTimeId, creationTime, and modificationTime on the floor. Calling components could not update local state with the new optimistic-concurrency values, so users saw stale data and had to refresh the page after every session-time edit. Fix is to return the API response from both helpers and have handleAddSession / handleUpdateSession capture and propagate sessionTimeId + creationTime + modificationTime into local React session state. This is the EMC-wide convention for any API helper that yields server-issued timestamps.

nodes.summary: RBAC scope attachment point: anchor at Series level, not Event, to enable transitive authorization through seriesId → scopeId resolution and efficient scope-based queries.
nodes.details: Series is the natural top-level container in the ownership hierarchy (Series → Events → Sessions); every resource transitively knows its scope through seriesId. Store scopeId two ways: (1) embedded in series itemData for efficient reads, (2) as a DynamoDB relationship item (pk: scope#<scopeId>, sk: series#<seriesId>) to enable KeyConditionExpression queries like getGroupsForScope. Child scope inheritance uses recursive getDescendantScopeIds(scopeId) enumerated at query time (hierarchy is shallow: platform → org → team). Authorization middleware: resolveAccessibleScopes resolves group → descendant scope IDs → req.userInfo.accessibleScopeIds; requireResourceScopeAccess(getResourceScopeIdFn) gates single-resource access by checking resource's resolved scopeId. Backwards compatibility: treat scopeId: null as pre-RBAC (open access); new resources get scopeId on creation; existing series migrated via PUT /v1/series/:seriesId/scope using TransactWriteCommand.

nodes.summary: Optimistic concurrency via modificationTime prevents lost updates on concurrent event edits
nodes.details: Implemented by be-agent-events: Every PUT /events/:id requires a modificationTime field matching the server's last-known value. If they differ, the update returns 409 Conflict with the current server state. The frontend shows a diff dialog allowing the user to merge or overwrite. This pattern prevents the classic 'last write wins' problem when two admins edit the same event.

nodes.summary: Scope configs unify RSVP forms, locales, and custom attributes under a single typed config system with scope-inherited hierarchy (org → team) and full-replace merge semantics.
nodes.details: All configuration for the events console — RSVP form fields, locale definitions, and custom attribute definitions — is managed through a single `/v1/scopes/{scopeId}/configs` API with `type` field (e.g., 'rsvp', 'locales', 'custom-attributes'). Configs inherit down the scope hierarchy with full-replace merge per type. Frontend reads merged configs via `GET /v1/events/{eventId}/configs` or `GET /v1/series/{seriesId}/configs` with optional `?type=` filter. Custom attributes are a config type, not a separate entity. Admin management uses POST/PUT/DELETE on `/v1/scopes/{scopeId}/configs/{configId}` and requires `config:read`, `config:write`, or `config:delete` permissions.

nodes.summary: Silent failures in Splash attendee status updates (PUT /external/events/:id/attendees/:id) due to missing externalAttendeeId → attendeeId mappings caused EMC/Splash count mismatches; resolved via direct DynamoDB correction.
nodes.details: When Splash sends status updates via PUT /external/events/:id/attendees/:id without a valid externalAttendeeId → attendeeId mapping in the service layer, the request fails silently rather than returning an error, leaving EMC counts stale while Splash reflects the true state. This caused deltas of 135+ waitlisted and 80+ declined records. Future agents should: (1) audit the attendee mapping lookup logic in the PUT handler to ensure it returns explicit errors on missing mappings rather than silently skipping updates, (2) add monitoring/alerting on PUT /external/events/:id/attendees/:id response codes to catch similar silent failures early, (3) recognize that zzTest migration scripts in this repo are the canonical runbook for data reconciliation when such mismatches occur.

nodes.summary: When hydrating event payloads from DynamoDB kinesis records with sk=localizations, source seriesId and detailPagePath from the pre-fetched liveData object, not from newData.itemData (which lacks these fields).
nodes.details: In EventDataStreamProcessor.js, when processing a localization record change (sk=localizations), the newData.itemData payload contains only localizations and localizationOverrides. To build a complete hydrated event for ESL, pull seriesId and detailPagePath from liveData (fetched via eventService.getEventData at processRecord start), not from newData.itemData. This is safe because EventService.updateVenue writes the new detailPagePath to DynamoDB before the venue record fires the kinesis stream, ensuring liveData.detailPagePath is current. Omitting these fields causes DA webhook page creation to fail or write to wrong locations.

nodes.summary: Do not omit detailPagePath from event PUT payloads; instead, use dataFilters to toggle submittable: true when title changes, coordinating with backend OpenAPI spec updates.
nodes.details: When updating an event via ESL PUT, detailPagePath was previously omitted because the backend marked it read-only. However, title changes require a new detailPagePath (new DA page). The fix: in useEventFormSave.ts, call dataFilters to set detailPagePath.submittable = true before the PUT, and detect title changes to trigger the DA page path dialog. This requires coordinated backend changes to the OpenAPI spec to allow the field in PUT requests. The anti-pattern is assuming a read-only field can never be submitted; instead, use conditional submittability flags in dataFilters based on business logic (e.g., title mutation).

nodes.summary: Event speaker PUT request body must be contract-shaped; do not spread raw GET response into PUT payload.
nodes.details: The API service layer enforces a specific payload shape for speaker PUT operations (web-src/src/services/api.ts). When updating event speakers, construct the request body to match the server's expected contract rather than spreading the GET response directly. This prevents field mismatches and validation failures. See Sessions and EventForm components for correct usage patterns.

nodes.summary: RSVP contactMethods field must not be spread directly from GET response into PUT payload; use prepareContactMethodsForPut helper to normalize shape.
nodes.details: The events-form block's RSVP submission was spreading the GET response contactMethods array directly into the PUT body, causing server-side validation failures when field shapes diverged between read and write contracts. The fix introduces a normalization step (prepareContactMethodsForPut in event-libs/v1/blocks/events-form/events-form.js) that maps the GET schema to the PUT schema before submission. This pattern applies to all ESP PUT operations: never assume GET and PUT payloads have identical field structures; always use a prepare* helper to bridge the contract gap.

nodes.summary: Do not replace entire itemData objects in DynamoDB PUT operations without preserving required fields; use merge/patch semantics or enforce all required fields in the request schema.
nodes.details: Publishing profiles were created with status: 'active', but PUT /v1/publishing-profiles/{profileId} requests that omitted status would replace the entire stored itemData, removing the field. This caused later GET /v1/events/{eventId}/publishing-profiles responses to fail OpenAPI validation (418 error) because status is a required field on PublishingProfile schema. Fix: (1) add defensive fallback in profile read paths to return status: 'active' if missing, (2) make status required on PublishingProfileUpdateRequest schema to prevent future drops, (3) ensure PublishingProfile response schema enforces status as required. This pattern applies to all DynamoDB-backed resources where PUT replaces rather than merges.

nodes.summary: EMC is a frontend-only ExC Shell SPA with no backend repo; all mutations and queries call external Adobe APIs (ESP, ESL) directly through a centralized ApiService with caching, validation, and dry-run support.
nodes.details: EMC (web-src/src/) is a React 18 + TypeScript + React Spectrum S2 SPA deployed via Adobe App Builder. There is no backend in this repo. All API calls route through services/api.ts (ApiService) and cachedApi wrapper: GET requests use 10s caching with request dedup and pattern-based invalidation; all mutations require input validation via validateString()/validateObject() before dispatch; all fetch calls pass through safeFetch() with ALLOWED_HOSTS validation. Two external backends: Adobe ESP (events/series/speakers endpoints) and ESL (lifecycle/venues/attendees). Auth uses Bearer token (IMS in prod, dev token locally) + x-gw-ims-org-id header. Dry-run mode available via apiService.enableDryRun(). Form state (EventForm, SeriesForm) persists to sessionStorage with debounced auto-save; multi-step FormWizard uses useEventFormComponent hook lifecycle (onGatherPayload, onAfterSave, onLoadResponse, validate) for step registration.

nodes.summary: Do not use Kinesis payload as source of truth for event metadata; always rehydrate from DynamoDB on every stream record, even for localization-only updates.
nodes.details: EMC emits two Kinesis records per event save (one for event, one for localization), but only the first carries full metadata (e.g., cloud-type). In EventDataStreamProcessor.js processRecord(), the prior logic conditionally rehydrated from DynamoDB only when liveUpdate=true, causing localization records to forward partial payloads downstream. This broke `.page` preview RSVP forms when the second (partial) write overwrote the first (complete) write. Fix: always rebuild newData.itemData from liveData (DynamoDB), falling back to Kinesis payload only for localizations and localizationOverrides fields. This ensures both eventData and localization Kinesis records produce fully hydrated payloads to Hoolihan/AIO DA.

nodes.summary: Speakers and sponsors are grouped by role/tier with per-group drag-and-drop reordering; role/tier changes move items to the end of the new group and trigger per-group ordinal recomputation.
nodes.details: In SpeakersComponent.tsx and SponsorsComponent.tsx, items are grouped by speakerType and tier respectively. Drag-and-drop is restricted to within-group moves only (cross-group drops are blocked). When a speaker's role or sponsor's tier is changed via inline picker, the item is moved to the end of the new group. On save, onAfterSave computes per-group ordinals for both components. SponsorData now includes an optional ordinal field, and updateSponsorInEvent in api.ts explicitly preserves ordinal in the merge logic. Both components display a disclaimer note that group display order on the DA page is governed by template configuration, not EMC form ordering.

nodes.summary: Parallel API queries for attendee status types are merged into a single result set; new status types require only type union updates and StatusBadge entries, not table/filter/export logic changes.
nodes.details: In EMC's Registrations page, attendee statuses (registered, waitlisted, declined) are fetched via parallel `?type=X` queries in `getAllEventAttendees()` (web-src/src/services/api.ts) and merged into a single `AttendeeStats` result. The `RegistrationStatus` type union (web-src/src/types/attendee.ts) controls which statuses exist. Adding a new status requires: (1) extending the `RegistrationStatus` union, (2) adding a `StatusBadge` variant entry (web-src/src/components/shared/StatusBadge.tsx), and (3) updating `AttendeeStats` interface. Table rendering, filtering, and CSV export are data-driven and automatically support new statuses without code changes.

recentUpdates.summary: Session time storage: UTC millis for persistence, naive ISO strings for API transport with IANA timezone
recentUpdates.details: Decision: all session start/end times stored as UTC millis in the database. API responses include naive ISO datetime strings (e.g., '2026-06-15T09:00:00') plus an IANA timezone string (e.g., 'America/Los_Angeles'). Two utility functions: naiveDateTimeToUTCMillis(naive, tz) and millisToNaiveDateTimeString(millis, tz). This separates display concerns from storage concerns.

recentUpdates.summary: Session form mockup: naive datetime inputs with explicit venue timezone selector
recentUpdates.details: Figma mockup for session creation form. Start/end time inputs show the time as it appears at the venue (naive). A timezone dropdown defaults to the venue's IANA timezone (derived from locationId). Users can override the timezone if the session is virtual. Auto-registration toggle below the time inputs. Speaker assignment section with search and change detection.

recentUpdates.summary: Session CRUD API complete — all endpoints use UTC millis, timezone conversion utilities tested
recentUpdates.details: Implemented POST/GET/PUT/DELETE /sessions endpoints. Create and update accept UTC millis for start/end with IANA timezone string. Response includes both UTC millis and naive datetime strings for frontend convenience. Speaker assignment handled via speakerIds array with originalSpeakerIds for change detection. Optimistic concurrency via creationTime/modificationTime comparison. locationId references venue locations table.

recentUpdates.summary: Session list view with timezone-aware display and venue location badges
recentUpdates.details: SessionListView renders sessions with venue-local times using millisToNaiveDateTimeString(). Each session row shows: title, naive start/end times, venue name badge, speaker count, auto-registration status icon. Sortable by start time (sorts on UTC millis). Pagination via cursor-based API.

recentUpdates.summary: Session creation form with naive datetime inputs — blocked on API contract for timezone conversion responsibility
recentUpdates.details: Session form has naive datetime inputs and venue timezone selector per design mockup. Speaker assignment with search and change detection (tracks originalSpeakerIds). Auto-registration toggle. Currently converting to UTC millis client-side before API call, but unsure if this is the agreed contract — backend API accepts UTC millis but design mockup implies the API should accept naive strings.

recentUpdates.summary: Proposal: auto-registration should default ON for new sessions
recentUpdates.details: Based on data from the current EMC: 78% of sessions at Adobe events have auto-registration enabled. Defaulting it ON saves organizers a click and matches the majority use case. Organizers creating invite-only or capacity-limited sessions can turn it off.

recentUpdates.summary: Recommends auto-registration default OFF — downstream webhook implications
recentUpdates.details: Responding to pm-configs. Auto-registration ON triggers a webhook to the registration service immediately on session create. If a session is created as a draft or accidentally, this creates registration records that require manual cleanup. The registration service has no 'undo' endpoint. Safer to default OFF and let organizers explicitly enable it when the session is finalized.
